_README: OPTIONAL hand-maintained provider notes: ToS posture + evidence class, keyed by the provider/wallet name buckets.sh assigns (matched case-insensitively against a bucket's `provider`, then its `local_providers`; first match wins). Never fetched at runtime - edit by hand whenever you learn something, or delete the file, and nothing breaks; `fa show`/`fa lanes -v` just stop printing the TOS line. tos: ok | caution | avoid | unknown. Seeded 2026-09-27 from OmniRoute's independent free-tier ToS catalog (github.com/diegosouzapw/OmniRoute, docs/reference/FREE_TIERS.md) - that is THEIR legal read of each provider's terms, not this project's; re-verify before leaning on it for anything that matters. A provider absent from this file has simply not been looked at yet, which is not the same as 'ok'.

openrouter.ai.note: OmniRoute's catalog rates OpenRouter 'caution'. This is fa's primary lane (kilo/openrouter.ai, see docs/dev/SESSION.md's lane table) - not a reason to stop using it, a reason to have actually read its terms before leaning on it hard.

openrouter.note: same wallet as openrouter.ai under a different local provider name - see that entry.

opencode.note: OmniRoute's own ToS catalog rates proxy/relay-style use of opencode's built-in free gateway 'avoid'. That is exactly the usage pattern of fa's own opencode-provider lane (see SESSION.md's lane table) - their independent read, not fa's; verify current terms yourself.

agy.note: same rating as opencode above, per OmniRoute's catalog. Not a lane on this machine yet - worth reading before adding one.

groq.note: ~30M/mo across five per-model caps; no payment method required at signup. Net-new candidate wallet - not yet reachable through any fa adapter without a hermes credential_pool entry or a hand-edited kilo.jsonc provider.

glm-cn.note: Z.AI / Zhipu - best ToS rating in OmniRoute's catalog. Uncapped + ~20M signup bonus. Net-new candidate; see 'zhipu'.

zhipu.note: same underlying account as glm-cn/glm in OmniRoute's catalog (they share one poolKey, zhipu-flash-free) - see glm-cn.

deepseek.note: one-time ~5M, no credit card required, 30-day expiry. Net-new candidate.

mistral.note: ~1B/mo - the single largest pool in OmniRoute's catalog - but its own terms scope free use to 'personal needs' only. Net-new candidate.

hyperbolic.note: one-time ~5M via a $1 trial credit. Net-new candidate.

nara.note: ~210M/mo - OmniRoute's own catalog leaves its ToS posture ambiguous rather than picking ok/caution/avoid. Net-new candidate; read its terms yourself before adding it.

xkiro.note: ~150M/mo shared across 39 models on one daily allowance. Net-new candidate.

llm7.note: ~150M/mo per OmniRoute's current catalog prose (a sibling constant in their own source is a stale, deprecated 4.3M figure - if this number is ever re-verified, trust their catalog file over that constant). Requires a free token from token.llm7.io. Net-new candidate.

cohere.note: ~800K/mo - OmniRoute notes its trial keys are 'not for production'. Net-new candidate.

nvidia.note: uncapped and genuinely keyless, but OmniRoute's catalog scopes it 'dev/eval only, not production'. Net-new candidate, zero signup friction.

stepfun.note: already one of the models on this machine's nous/hermes lane (see docs/dev/SESSION.md's lane table) - not a new wallet, just a terms note on an existing one.
